# Generative AI and Large Language Models

Teach capabilities and limitations together. Distinguish model behavior from
system behavior, and require evaluation for real deployments.

## Foundations

- Language models, tokenization, context windows, and generation.
- Transformer architecture and attention.
- Embeddings, semantic search, and vector indexes.
- Prompt design, grounding, and hallucination risks.

## Applications

- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and chunking.
- Fine-tuning and parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA.
- Evaluation, safety, and quality measurement.
- Tool calling, agents, MCP, and multi-agent workflows.
- Deployment, latency, cost, privacy, and observability.

## Practice and review

- Compare retrieval and fine-tuning for a stated use case.
- Measure retrieval quality separately from answer quality.
- Identify privacy, prompt injection, access-control, and data-retention risks.
- Never claim model output is factually correct without suitable verification.
